title: Campaign Manager
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is seeking an Enterprise Integrated Campaign Manager to design, orchestrate, scale, and measure integrated marketing campaigns that support our Enterprise business priorities and drive demand, adoption, and expansion across customer segments, from small businesses to large enterprises. As a key member of our marketing organization, you'll build the campaign frameworks and cross-channel motions that connect our content, physical events, digital programs, and account-based efforts into cohesive journeys that move buyers from awareness to activation.

This role requires a sophisticated understanding of B2B marketing with demonstrated success in integrated campaign strategy and execution across the full customer lifecycle. You'll develop and execute comprehensive campaign strategies in partnership with Sales, Field Marketing, Product Marketing, Partner Marketing, and Digital teams, creating compelling programs and flywheel motions that help Sales teams reach their pipeline and revenue targets.

Enterprise represents one of our largest growth opportunities and our most nuanced challenge, a segment where long sales cycles, complex buying committees, and industry-specific requirements demand campaigns that are deeply orchestrated rather than one-size-fits-all. You'll work closely with Product and Field Marketing, the broader Integrated Campaigns team, and cross-functional partners to ensure campaigns directly support demand generation, customer adoption, and strategic account expansion.

We're hiring several campaign managers, with focus areas including Scale (high-volume demand and adoption campaigns for SMB and Commercial customers), Customer Marketing (campaigns built on customer stories), and Industries. You don't need experience in every area. If one or more fits your background, tell us in your application.

Key responsibilities

  • Design and lead integrated campaigns across customer segments, establishing scalable frameworks and processes that connect digital, events, content, and ABM channels into cohesive buyer journeys
  • Drive full-funnel campaign initiatives across core priorities, industries, segments, and regions, adapting strategies to how each audience buys, from self-serve and small teams to enterprise buying committees
  • Create and implement campaign programs including thought leadership moments, digital nurture streams, webinar series, executive engagement programs, and ABM activations
  • Partner closely with Field Marketing to align campaign programs with territory and account-specific goals that directly achieve pipeline, adoption, and expansion targets
  • Optimize programs using measurement frameworks, including lead scoring, attribution models, and ROI reporting to demonstrate campaign impact on demand, adoption, and revenue
  • Collaborate with global Marketing teams to ensure Enterprise campaigns align with company-wide strategy while meeting segment- and industry-specific needs
  • Coordinate with Product Marketing and Solutions Marketing to ensure consistent messaging and positioning across all campaign touchpoints
  • Work with Customer Marketing to build campaigns around customer stories, with customer approvals planned into the timeline
  • Direct media and creative agencies, and manage vendors and internal creative and content teams, keeping briefs, timelines, and approvals moving so programs are delivered on time and on budget
  • Build and manage campaign budgets with strong financial discipline and ROI focus
  • Drive continuous improvement through post-campaign analysis, stakeholder feedback, and data-driven optimization

Minimum qualifications

  • Demonstrate deep understanding of how businesses buy software, through enterprise buying committees or high-volume and self-serve models - experience working within software companies is required for this position
  • Have a track record of successfully building and scaling integrated campaign programs that span digital, events, content, and ABM or lifecycle channels
  • Have strong analytical skills and a data-driven approach to campaign optimization and attribution
  • Have demonstrated success in contributing to significant demand, adoption, and revenue goals through integrated marketing initiatives
  • Are a proven self-starter who can build and run sophisticated programs with small teams in fast-paced startup environments
  • Have strong project management skills, with experience managing several multi-channel campaigns and agencies at once, for different audiences
  • Possess strong budgeting and financial management capabilities with experience managing substantial campaign budgets
  • Excel at cross-functional collaboration, particularly with sales teams, agency partners, and executive stakeholders
  • Are comfortable with ambiguity and thrive in fast-paced, evolving environments with a bias for thoughtful action

Preferred qualifications

  • Have 10+ years of B2B marketing experience with expertise in integrated campaigns and demand generation, plus depth in account-based, lifecycle, or customer marketing
  • Have experience marketing AI/ML or complex technical products to enterprise customers
  • Have experience building and leading integrated campaign or demand generation teams
  • Have deep knowledge of account-based marketing (ABM) strategies and execution, including platforms such as 6sense or Demandbase
  • Have experience at high-growth technology companies
  • Have experience developing industry- or segment-specific campaign motions for regulated or vertical markets
  • Have run B2B campaigns built on customer stories, including working with customers' brand, comms, and legal teams on approvals
  • Have run high-volume demand, lifecycle, or self-serve campaigns for small business or mid-market customers
  • Have marketing automation and campaign operations fluency (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce) with an understanding of lead lifecycle management
  • Have international campaign experience and an understanding of how to localize programs across regions, including EMEA

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$255,000—$320,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. title: Head of Campaign Operations
description:

About the role

Anthropic is looking for a Head of Campaign Operations to build the tools, processes, and insights for what our enterprise campaigns need to plan, deploy, and drive impact. This role spans our audience campaigns, as well as the channel teams with whom we work to deliver campaigns: paid media, social media, webinars, email, web, content, and more. You'll own how work comes in, gets planned, gets built, launches, and gets measured.

This is a player-coach role. You'll lead a small team of full-time employees and contractors, and you'll build alongside them: the intake, templates, calendars, tools, reporting, and ways of working that let campaign and content leads spend their time on strategy and delivery. Ultimately, you are responsible for building an efficient and automated campaign supply chain that can grow from today's programs to a global operation across regions, languages, and time zones.

The ideal candidate holds an equal mix of campaign strategy, operational expertise, and analytical capability.

You'll report to the Head of Enterprise Integrated Campaigns, and partner closely with the Head of Campaigns and the Head of Content Marketing.   • Have built campaign operating models from scratch, with intake, SLAs, calendars, reporting, and reviews that teams kept using
  • Have grown campaign operations from an early stage to global scale, and have run them day to day across multiple regions, languages, and time zones
  • Understand how integrated campaigns work end to end, and how paid media, web, email, webinars, events, and content fit together
  • Are performance minded, with a strong grasp of campaign measurement and the ability to build and interpret reporting when the data is imperfect
  • Have managed agencies through RFPs, SOWs, and large projects

title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Post-Training — Collective Alignment (User Signals)
description: About the Team The Collective Alignment (User Signals) team is a post-training research team working at the intersection of data science, human feedback, and reinforcement learning. We develop methods for learning from real-world user interactions to build AI systems that deliver lasting value, helping people learn, grow, and accomplish increasingly complex goals with ChatGPT. Learning from user feedback presents fundamental research challenges: signals are often noisy, biased, and difficult to interpret, and improvements in offline metrics do not always translate into better experiences for users. Our team develops scientific approaches to understanding these signals and translating them into improvements in model behavior through evaluations, reward modeling, and post-training. About the Role As a Research Engineer or Research Scientist, you will investigate how AI systems can learn from human feedback and real-world usage to better serve users over time. You will develop new approaches to extracting meaningful learning signals from complex user interactions and incorporating those signals into model training. This role requires strong deep learning research skills, scientific rigor, and curiosity about how people interact with AI. You will design controlled experiments and ablations, critically examine the relationship between offline evaluations and online model behavior, and work closely with research, product, and data science teams to understand whether improvements translate into meaningful value for users. In this role, you will: Develop novel methods for learning from human feedback and user interaction signals. Research approaches to incorporating feedback into reward modeling, reinforcement learning, and post-training. Design rigorous experiments and ablation studies to isolate the effects of new data, objectives, and training methods. Develop offline evaluations and investigate their relationship with online experiments and real-world user outcomes. Analyze unexpected results, investigate discrepancies between evaluation metrics and user behavior, and develop hypotheses to guide further research. Evaluate tradeoffs and regressions to improve targeted model behaviors while preserving broader capabilities. Collaborate with research, alignment, product, and data science teams. Implement and debug experiments across large-scale deep learning research systems. You might thrive in this role if you: Have a strong background in deep learning research through academic or industry experience. Have demonstrated research ability through publications or substantive research contributions in deep learning or LLM post-training. Have experience developing new machine learning methods and evaluating them through rigorous, hypothesis-driven experimentation. Think critically about experimental design, measurement, and what evaluation results do and do not establish about model behavior. Are comfortable designing ablations, investigating surprising results, and reasoning about the relationship between offline metrics and real-world outcomes. Have strong programming skills and experience working with complex ML codebases. Are curious about how people interact with AI and how those interactions can inform better models. Nice to have: Experience with RLHF, reinforcement learning, or modern LLM post-training. Research or demonstrated interest in AI alignment, human feedback, or user signals. Experience with online experimentation, evaluation methodology, or learning from noisy and biased feedback. Experience connecting machine learning research with real-world product behavior. title: Research Engineer/Research Scientist- Post Training, Model Experience
description: About the Team The Post Training team is responsible for training and improving pre-trained models to be deployed into ChatGPT, the API, and potential future products. In the Model Experience team, we shape the default character and behavior of ChatGPT: how the model communicates, responds to users, uses its capabilities, and behaves across different contexts and languages. Our goal is to make every interaction with ChatGPT thoughtful, helpful, and trustworthy. We take an opinionated view of what good human–AI interaction should look like, then turn that vision into real model behavior through human data, evaluations, reward models, and post-training. Our work sits at the intersection of research, product, and model design. We partner closely with teams across OpenAI to conduct research and ensure our models are thoughtful, safe, reliable to serve millions of users. About the Role As a Research Engineer / Scientist, you will research and develop improvements to our models. Our team works in research areas combining reinforcement learning and products. We're looking for individuals with strong ML engineering skills and research experience, especially with novel and highly capable models. An ideal candidate is passionate about product-driven research and the quality of human-AI interaction. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Own and pursue a research agenda to improve model capability and performance. Collaborate closely with the other research and product teams, allowing customers to optimize their own models. Build robust evaluations for tracking modeling improvements. Design, implement, test, and debug code across our research stack. You might thrive in this role if you: Have a deep understanding of machine learning and machine learning applications. Have good judgment about model behavior and can communicate this judgment effectively. Enjoy taking ambitious, qualitative problems and turning them into concrete training interventions. Have a working knowledge of relevant models, and building evaluations for model capability improvement. Are comfortable diving into a large ML codebase to debug. Thrive in a dynamic, technically complex, and collaborative environment. title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Human Flourishing
description: About the Team The Human Flourishing team’s mission is to ensure AI systems understand and advance human flourishing. As AI becomes more capable and plays a larger role in people’s lives, we want its human benefits to grow with its capabilities. The Human Flourishing team is part of the broader Post Training organization. Our approach has two parts. Firstly, we measure and improve models’ understanding, capability, and propensity to act according to people’s values and to help them achieve their long-term goals. Secondly, we directly scale tangible impact for users in human domains like education and mental health, working across research, product, and partnerships to increase the benefits over a billion people experience weekly when they use ChatGPT. Our recent work includes Beneficial RL , which investigates how training for beneficial behavior generalizes across settings, and MentalHealthBench , a benchmark developed with mental health experts to evaluate realistic conversations. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher to turn difficult-to-define signals of long-term flourishing into measurable improvements in model behavior. You’ll help set research direction, build what is needed to test your ideas, and drive successful work into the models and products we ship. We’re especially interested in researchers with deep experience improving frontier models through pretraining or reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, especially on less verifiable problems, or researchers who combine strong LLM skills with deep expertise in domains like education or mental health. Prior experience in these domains is not required. In this role, you will Develop scalable training methods across the training stack that improve how models understand people’s values, support their agency, and help them achieve long-term goals. Lead high-leverage research from an open question to a shipped improvement: choose a hard-to-define problem, iteratively define success, run experiments, and integrate into frontier models. Build RL environments for difficult-to-verify outcomes, and study whether beneficial behavior generalizes across settings. Create evaluations grounded in human expertise and feedback that reveal capability gaps, unintended incentives in RL, and failures that aggregate scores can miss. Test whether measures of model behavior predict better learning, wellbeing, and other long-term outcomes, and use those findings to guide training. Build new 0→1 capabilities in human domains that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. Partner with product teams, engineers, partnerships teams, and domain experts to deploy promising methods, measure their effects in real use, and turn what you learn into further improvements. Assess AI’s impacts on human flourishing at the scale of over a billion users. You might thrive in this role if you Care deeply about helping AI improve people’s lives, and feel this is a responsibility that comes with increasingly capable models. Have an unusually strong research record in pretraining or RL / post-training research, especially in a hard-to-verify area; or combine strong LLM research skills with deep expertise in education, mental health, or a related field of human benefit. Are a hands-on builder who can turn ideas into rigorous experiments, write and debug code, and work directly with data and training infrastructure. Have the taste to choose consequential problems and actionable steps on the path to solving those problems. Take ownership of ambiguous problems and choose methods based on the impact they can deliver, including when the most useful work is unglamorous. Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. Work well across disciplines and can grok the most important bottlenecks to scaling our impact in a multidisciplinary problem. If you’re excited about ensuring AI systems advance human flourishing, we’d love to hear from you. title: Research Engineer / Research Scientist, Health
description: About the Team The Health team, within OpenAI’s broader Post Training organization, has a mission to ensure AGI improves health for all humanity. Improving human health will be one of the defining impacts of AGI. Hundreds of millions of people already turn to ChatGPT for questions about their health and millions of clinicians use it weekly to support care delivery. Increasingly capable models create an opportunity to make high-quality medical intelligence more accessible across patients and clinicians—raising the floor of human health—and accelerate the new capabilities and scientific advances that raise the ceiling of human health. Our job is to make those benefits real. We work across the full model stack—pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, post-training, evaluations, harnessing, and deployment—and connect that research to the patients, clinicians, and real-world outcomes we aim to improve. About the Role We’re looking for an exceptional, hands-on researcher who wants to build frontier health capabilities and turn them into impact at scale. This is a role for someone who can take an important, underdefined problem from 0→1: identify the right bet, build what’s needed to test it, and drive it all the way to a measurable improvement in the models and products we actually ship. We’re especially excited about two kinds of people: researchers with the technical depth to move the frontier in pretraining, reinforcement learning (RL) / post-training, or evals; and researchers with real depth in developing frontier biomedical AI capabilities. Prior experience in healthcare is helpful but not required. Research excellence, velocity, ownership, and alignment with the mission are most important to us. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: Own a high-leverage research direction end to end—from deciding which problem matters and how to measure it, to designing and running experiments, to integrating successful work into frontier models. Develop scalable methods across pretraining, midtraining, reinforcement learning, and post-training to improve health reasoning, knowledge, reliability, calibration, and behavior. Build and study RL environments grounded in real health problems; understand which data and training setups produce robust, generalizable improvements rather than just higher benchmark scores. Create meaningful, trustworthy, and unsaturated evaluations that tell us whether our models are actually getting better at what matters for patients and clinicians. Advance new 0→1 capabilities in health that may have an increasing impact with upcoming increases in model intelligence and test-time compute. Develop models and agents that can work over longitudinal, multimodal health data to produce useful predictions, surface new scientific insights, and support better individual- and population-level decisions. Work closely with researchers, engineers, clinicians, and product teams to bring health capabilities into the models and products used by hundreds of millions of people. Help establish that AI improves real health outcomes, not just that it can produce impressive answers or demos. You might thrive in this role if you: Care deeply about using increasingly capable AI to improve human health, and take seriously the responsibility of deploying it safely. Have an unusually strong track record in machine learning or AI research, with the depth to push at least one important area forward: pretraining, reinforcement learning / post-training, evals (not necessarily specific to health); or substantial depth in a relevant frontier health / biomedical AI problem. Are a hands-on builder: you can design experiments, write and debug code, work directly with data and training infrastructure, and move quickly from an idea to evidence. Have strong research taste and can distinguish an important problem or a promising approach from an interesting one. Own ambiguous problems end to end, and are willing to learn whatever is missing to get the job done. Stay goal-oriented rather than method-oriented, and don’t shy away from unglamorous work if it is the highest-leverage path to impact. Care about whether a capability will scale, generalize, and make it into the real world—not just whether it can be shown in a paper or prototype. Enjoy working with low-ego, ambitious people across research, engineering, medicine, and product. Bonus: Experience with health AI, longitudinal health data, or clinical research. If you want your work to help make medical intelligence widely accessible—and to work on some of the most important frontier problems at the intersection of AI, science, and human health—we’d love to hear from you.
